question: Q1: In adult humans, what are the bony attachments of the pectoralis major, which glenohumeral joint actions does each of its clavicular and sternocostal portions contribute to, and does the relative contribution vary with humeral position? Q2: In healthy adults performing supervised resistance training, does a programme using the barbell flat bench press differ from one using the bilateral standing cable fly at shoulder height in pectoralis major hypertrophy, and secondarily in task-specific maximal strength, when training variables are equated or reported?

synthesis:
SBLA-009 evidence packet, version 2.0.0, rebuilt in the R1 bounded remediation against reviews/evidence/SBLA-009-r1.md at 8154f1167062403a96ee5d6ec0fc63bd50ebfd17.

RECONCILIATION. unique records after deduplication = excluded + awaiting-full-text + included : 1956 = 1842 + 26 + 88. records retrieved = duplicates + unique records after deduplication : 2343 = 387 + 1956. Duplicates are deduplication events, not exclusions; an awaiting-full-text record is neither included nor excluded. The sum of exclusionCodeCounts equals 1842, the excluded total.

Q2, THE PRIMARY QUESTION, HAS NO ANSWER AND THIS PACKET DOES NOT MANUFACTURE ONE. No study of the index condition — the bilateral standing cable fly at shoulder height as frozen in research/questions/SBLA-008-vertical-slice.md section 3.2 — was retrieved by any route this project ran, and no study comparing a barbell flat bench press with any cable fly for a pectoralis major size outcome was retrieved. Both absences are recorded as absence of evidence within the routes actually run, never as equivalence or ineffectiveness, and both are now bound to the retrieval that produced them rather than stated universally.

THE ABSENCE NOW RESTS ON OPENED DOCUMENTS. The R1 review established that the single record this pass had itself called the most directly relevant press-versus-fly source had never been opened. It has been. G1016 (Schanke 2012, MSc thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse) was obtained from the MINDS@UW institutional repository without authentication — 21,237,276 bytes, sha256 81a2a094349a0fccd822247cf2d36b08449bffe2035d30869521049c2dc6a950 — and read in full. Its bent-forward cable crossover is described in the Methods with the arms at chest height and parallel to the floor, but the pulley origin height is never stated, and Figure 2 depicts handles above shoulder height with a downward-and-inward path. Under the frozen section 3.2 attribute table the pulley origin is a defining attribute of index Y and high-to-low crossover is a named distinct condition, so it is a related condition. Index Y remains unstudied, and the pass can now say so from a document it read.

EXTERNAL CORROBORATION OF THE ABSENCE. An independent 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis of pectoralis major EMG in the bench press and other pectoral exercises (DOI 10.3390/app13085203, CC BY 4.0) searched PubMed/MEDLINE, SPORTDiscus and Web of Science to 25 March 2023 — two databases this project cannot search — hand-screened every selected article's reference list, identified 951 publications and included 23 studies. Its six exercise-type comparisons are against push-ups, dumbbell exercises, elastic resistance and a chest press. No cable fly appears anywhere in it. That is stronger evidence of absence than this project's own search can be.

WHAT THE PASS DOES CARRY. 23 draft claims and 5 explicit absence records, drawn from 88 included sources. The best-corroborated finding is regional differentiation within the pectoralis major. Two claims were re-derived in this remediation. claim-bench-press-inclination-shifts-regional-activation loses its monotonic wording and drops from moderate to low: the sternocostal decrease with inclination is consistent, but the clavicular response is not, with a measured peak near 30 degrees, reduced pectoralis performance above 45 degrees, a whole-contraction null, and a pooled clavicular null at p = 0.81 with I-squared 92.6 per cent. claim-press-versus-fly-activation-mixed is rebuilt on four primary comparisons plus a meta-analysis and is held at very-low: three of the four are null, none of the comparators is index Y, the one comparison reporting a difference did not normalise its EMG, and the pooled estimates carry I-squared of 94.9 and 98 per cent. A post-hoc amendment may lower certainty and may not raise it.

ACQUISITION IS NOW AN AUDITABLE STAGE. The eligibility-plan section 4.5 ladder was executed and recorded with its date and HTTP result for every record whose eligibility could turn on it. No record held awaiting-full-text or included at a lower access level carries an empty ladder. Nine sources moved from abstract-only or metadata-only to full-text-open once the ladder reached PubMed Central or a repository rather than stopping at the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint; no source remains at metadata-only. Where a host refused this client the status code is recorded and the ladder moved to the next lawful rung: no paywall was circumvented, no user-agent was substituted, and no shadow library was accessed.

LIMITS THAT REMAIN. The search is not exhaustive: 11,765 PubMed composite records across S1 to S4 against a screened set of 1956. Cochrane CENTRAL was not searched, and no access control was circumvented to reach it. SPORTDiscus and Web of Science were not searched by this project, and the gap is mitigated by citing the 2023 review rather than closed by searching. Forward citation chasing is truncated at 200 citing works per seed, and a pre-specified relevance expression reduced 3,479 chased works to 841 before screening. 26 records remain awaiting full text, each with a dated ladder. Screening of the 848 records added by the remediation used a disclosed two-pass method whose first pass is a deterministic rule set that can only exclude. Double screening on a separate day was not performed. Every one of these is stated in the synthesis and appraisal limitation sections rather than left for a reviewer to find.

Adopted retrieval rule R-RULE-1 before opening any record: route-level composite counts are recorded for all six PubMed composites, but the record set entering screening is defined by six pre-specified PubMed retrieval strata plus the complete yield of the Europe PMC fly-family route, the ClinicalTrials.gov Essie route, ten quoted-phrase OpenAlex probes and the preprint routes. The residual recall gap is quantified per route in the search receipts and carried as limitation L-1. Reason: S1 to S4 alone return 11,765 records, which cannot be screened record by record with a recorded reason in one session, and silently screening a convenience subset would be worse than declaring the rule.

Carried the historical Europe PMC E1 count of 334 from 2026-09-11 into the search receipts as receipt R-001, labelled historical and not re-executed, and executed the amended E1 string fresh on 2026-09-13: 397 for the same 1960-01-01 to 2026-09-11 window and 398 with the window extended to the execution date. Three rows, three provenances. The prerequisite decision required exactly this.

Amendment AM-2 to the deduplication rule: registered the normalised-title fuzzy key for every record rather than only for identifier-less records, because a PubMed record keyed by PMID and an index record with no identifier can never merge under an identifier-only rule. Eleven additional merges resulted; all thirteen fuzzy-only merges were inspected individually and confirmed. Recorded in the screening-flow companion.

Amendment AM-1 to the exclusion reason codes under eligibility plan section 6.2 and assumption EA1: added E-REC-5, E-REC-6, E-REC-7 (reserved, not issued), E-EXP-7 and E-DES-6. Made after results were visible and therefore flagged post-hoc. Each new code is administrative or classificatory, none removes a record that an existing substantive code would have retained, and none can raise certainty.

Applied eligibility plan section 4.5 strictly: an eligible record whose only admissible contribution is a tier-1 or tier-2 longitudinal outcome, and whose full text was not lawfully obtained, is awaiting-full-text and not included. That moved ten tier-1 trials out of the included set. The rule cost this pass most of its hypertrophy evidence and was applied anyway, because a tier-1 estimate taken from an abstract cannot be checked for measurement site, timing, equating or reliability.

Classified the cable cross-over condition in the only same-participants press-versus-cable mechanics study as a related condition rather than index Y, because pulley height, elbow-angle prescription and stance are all unreported. Eligibility plan section 2.3 rule 3 resolves two or more unreported defining attributes away from the index set. Consequence: the slice has no index-Y measurement of any kind.

Ran the section 9.7 status check on all 76 included sources against the Crossref REST API per-DOI update fields and the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched on 2026-09-13. One source is corrected (the glenohumeral moment-arm systematic review, erratum DOI 10.1111/joa.13417). The erratum could not be read because the publisher returned HTTP 403 to this client, so no number from that review is carried into any claim. Two retracted records were found in the contradiction stratum and blocked.

Did not substitute a user agent to reach any Cochrane URL, and did not attempt any workaround of the Wiley, Elsevier, ScienceDirect, MDPI or NATA edge blocks. C1 is recorded as not executed, with the narrow client-specific reason and three dated status codes. This closes SBLA-008 R2 finding M-10 with a narrower statement than the one it flagged.

Reported the absence of index-Y evidence as absence and did not widen Y, did not pool a related condition into the primary comparison, and drafted no press-versus-fly hypertrophy claim. Anti-cherry-picking rule 7 and the frozen U2/EU2 decision both require this, and the search receipts record the six routes that would have found such a study.

R1 REMEDIATION, C-1. Executed the eligibility-plan section 4.5 acquisition ladder, with its date and HTTP result, for every record that carried an empty or partial ladder: 24 awaiting-full-text records and 52 included records below full-text-open. Recorded every attempt as a structured {step, route, url, attemptedAt, result} object rather than opaque text, so that no absence or completeness statement rests on a record nobody tried to open.

R1 REMEDIATION, C-1. Obtained and read G1016, the record the first pass had itself called the most directly relevant press-versus-fly source and had never attempted to retrieve. Promoted it from awaiting-full-text to included. Its cable condition is a high-to-low crossover with an unstated pulley origin, so index Y remains unstudied — but that is now a finding from a read document rather than an assumption.

R1 REMEDIATION, I-2 and I-4. Added backward and forward citation chasing over the included set, which the first pass omitted entirely despite master plan section 9.6 naming it a primary discovery channel, and added the 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis it recovers. Chasing produced 3,559 distinct candidate works; a pre-specified relevance expression retained 841, of which 745 were new and were screened to a terminal state.

R1 REMEDIATION, I-6. Added non-English exercise vocabulary to the OpenAlex and Europe PMC routes and used the DOAJ public article API. Both records the R1 report named as demonstrated recall losses were retrieved. One of them, a Portuguese comparison of the barbell bench press with a machine fly in 13 trained men, is now an included source and carries an authorised English abstract, so it needed no machine translation.

R1 REMEDIATION, I-6 and deduplication. The DOAJ record established that the English-titled record held as G1006 and the Portuguese-titled record held as G1022 are the same 2014 RBPFEX report: identical author list, identical year, identical publisher URL, and one bilingual abstract carrying both titles. Merged as a deduplication event, never as an exclusion. This is a defect completed retrieval exposed, not one the review was asked to find.

R1 REMEDIATION, I-13. Added the amended portion-terminology stratum N-RS4a and a bench-angle stratum N-RS7. Between them they recovered five of the six PMIDs the R1 report named as absent, including both studies that contradict the inclination claim as it was first worded.

R1 REMEDIATION, honesty over inclusion count. Four records adjudicated eligible on their titles were held at awaiting-full-text rather than counted as included, because no abstract and no full text could be obtained for them by any lawful route and nothing can be extracted from a record whose content was never obtained. Eligibility-plan section 4.5 reserves inclusion for records whose content was actually obtained.

R1 REMEDIATION, I-12 and M-3. Corrected nine access levels from abstract-only or metadata-only to full-text-open after the ladder reached PubMed Central or a repository rather than stopping at the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint, which returns 404 for these records. Corrected the claim qualifier that asserted normalisation, electrode placement and crosstalk handling could not be verified: all three are in the full text, and the study did not normalise its EMG at all, which is a material limitation the first pass recorded as unverifiable.

Donor age and sex are stated for both cadaveric series (51 +/- 14 years, 9 male and 5 female; and mean 69.3 +/- 11.8 years, range 48 to 90). Recording the second lowered the applicability grade of claim-pectoralis-major-structural-variation from partially-direct to indirect, which is the point of recording it.

Bound every universal absence statement to the retrieval that produced it, in the absence records and in the reader-facing fly draft, and cited the 2023 review as external corroboration. An existence claim is not something this retrieval design can support; a statement about what these routes retrieved is.
